glosses: To stir together.

examples.text: Mix the eggs and milk with the flour until the consistency is smooth.

glosses: To combine (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).

examples.text: to mix business with pleasure
Don't mix the meat recipes with the dairy recipes.

glosses: To blend by the use of a mixer (machine).

examples.text: Mix the egg whites until they are stiff.

examples.text: Now add the raisins to the mix.

glosses: A preparation, usually in the form of a powder, into which other ingredients can be mixed to prepare a specified foodstuff.

examples.text: Cake mix. Pancake mix. Hot chocolate mix.

glosses: The result of mixing several tracks.

examples.text: The rhythm mix sounds muddy.

glosses: The finished version of a recording.

examples.text: I've almost finished the mix for this song.

glosses: A substance used to dilute or adulterate an illicit drug.

examples.text: Eventually I could taste different drugs and tell how much mix in it or if there’s too much mix in it or what have you.

glosses: To mix or blend thoroughly and completely.

examples.text: She mixed up peat moss, humus, and compost to make potting soil.

glosses: To combine thoroughly.

examples.text: All the smells of the food had mixed up together.

glosses: To prepare something from ingredients that are mixed.

examples.text: She mixed up a batch of her own potting soil.

glosses: To confuse or reverse.

examples.text: I always mix up Vermont and New Hampshire on a map.

glosses: To become involved with, especially socially or romantically.

examples.text: He got mixed up with a bad crowd.
Then he got mixed up with an older woman.

examples.text: Next time, let's ask a group with a different mix up.

examples.text: I refuse to send them any more money until they fix this mix up.

glosses: A mixture of two or more things.

examples.text: Their music has been described as a blend of jazz and heavy metal.
Our department has a good blend of experienced workers and young promise.

glosses: A word formed by combining two other words; a grammatical contamination, portmanteau word.

examples.text: Blends, also known as portmanteau words, are not an original part of English. That is, none occur in Old or Middle English, nor even in Elizabethan English, with the earliest known example being the rare and now obsolete term tomaxe, a blend of tomahawk and axe.

glosses: To mingle; to mix; to unite intimately; to pass or shade insensibly into each other.

examples.text: To make hummus you need to blend chickpeas, olive oil, lemon juice and garlic.

glosses: To be mingled or mixed.

examples.text: There is a tone of solemn and sacred feeling that blends with our conviviality.

Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close[…]above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them. Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.
